title: Solvents and Degreasers
summary: Solvents thin or dissolve paint, grease, epoxies, adhesives, and coatings. They can harm your health when breathed in, absorbed through the skin, or swallowed, and they are flammable.
talking_points: Check the product label or Safety Data Sheet (SDS) to find out if a product contains a solvent that could harm you.
Common solvents include acetone, MEK, toluene, xylene, mineral spirits, turpentine, and denatured alcohols.
OSHA requires employers to train workers who use hazardous chemicals and to provide protective equipment.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves, long sleeves, and eye protection.
Use a NIOSH-approved respirator with the correct, color-coded cartridge for the chemical.
If solvent gets on your skin, wash right away with soap and water. Do not wash your hands with a solvent, even if they are covered in paint.
Make sure the work area is ventilated. Employers must provide proper ventilation.
Solvents are flammable. Keep them away from electrical hazards, heat, and other fire-starting hazards. Ask if a water-based product can be used instead.
site_hazards_to_check: Bare hands used to scrub tools or brushes in solvent
Poor ventilation where solvents are used
Solvents near electrical equipment, heat, or other ignition sources
Products with no label or SDS to identify the solvent
Workers without chemical-resistant gloves, eye protection, or a respirator with the right cartridge
Confined spaces entered with no competent person checking that the space is safe
discussion_questions: Mary cleaned brushes with thinner using bare hands and ended up with red, dry, cracked skin. What caused this, and how could it be prevented?
Has anyone you know been hurt or made sick by solvents? What happened?
What will we do at the worksite today to prevent exposure to solvents?
